business_problem: Red Bull Advanced Technologies and the Red Bull Driver Academy needed a more precise way to show young drivers why one driver is faster than another, because coaches had limited tools to analyze braking, acceleration, gear changes, and racing lines from video with the accuracy required for high-performance driver development.
solution_summary: Red Bull Advanced Technologies worked with Oracle data science experts to build an AI-based driver analysis workflow on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI). The implementation starts by ingesting racing video, initially from Red Bull esports simulators, into OCI. Oracle’s team then applies simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) methods plus convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and recurrent neural networks (RNNs) to process frames, estimate visual odometry, determine on-track position, and infer car controls such as steering and wheel behavior. OCI Compute, including GPU-backed capacity, is used to run the most computationally intensive model-fitting and parameter-testing jobs, sometimes in parallel and sometimes over multiple days. The architecture splits processing into three parallel workflows for velocity/orientation, track location, and controls analysis, with the intended serving layer being an OCI-hosted application that accepts a driver session video and returns lap-by-lap and driver-to-driver performance insights for coaching.

solution_components.name: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI)
solution_components.role: Hosts the end-to-end video analysis workflow, from ingesting footage to refining models and running the planned driver analysis application.

solution_components.name: OCI Compute
solution_components.role: Provides the compute environment for the three parallel AI workflows that assess visual odometry, track location, and car controls.

solution_components.name: OCI graphics processor units (GPUs)
solution_components.role: Supply on-demand accelerated compute for AI modeling, parameter testing, and large experimental runs.

data_flow: Video footage from Red Bull esports simulators is ingested into OCI, then routed into three parallel workflows to estimate visual odometry, on-track location, and car controls. CNN and RNN models process the imagery, while OCI Compute and GPUs run parameter fitting and validation against on-track reality. The intended output is an OCI-based application that takes session video and returns coaching analysis on lap-to-lap and driver-to-driver differences.
integration_points: Red Bull Driver Academy coaching workflows
business_outcome: The project established an early-stage AI training workflow on OCI that lets the team run large numbers of experiments to improve model precision, with the goal of delivering deeper driver coaching analysis from video.
